newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Ekeus says his Iraq commission strapped for cash.
newsitem.headline: Ekeus says his Iraq commission strapped for cash.

text.p: The U.N. official in charge of eliminating Iraq's weapons of mass destruction said on Sunday his commission could be forced to close due to lack of funds.

"We told the (U.N.) Security Council that by the end of the year we are very short, almost all our funds are exhausted and that means we would have to close our operations," Rolf Ekeus told reporters in Kuwait before leaving for Saudi Arabia.
Diplomats earlier said Ekeus was on a Gulf Arab tour to secure funds for his commission, which was set up after the 1991 Gulf War to end Iraq's mass destruction arms capability.
Ekeus said his commission needed $30 million for 1997.
The cash problem is "very sensitive and difficult", said Ekeus, warning that if his commission is closed "there will no longer be any control on Iraq's" military programmes.
Ekeus said he had discussed the issue with some European powers and Washington while Kuwait had expressed during his three-day visit "principle readiness to support".
Ekeus last year went on a similar Gulf Arab tour ahead of an annual Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit to ask for $90 million over three years to finance his commission.
Diplomats said Ekeus would reiterate during the tour the need for financial contributions for his commission by Gulf Arab states who will hold their 1996 summit in Qatar in December.
The last summit said Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain would extend political and financial support but did not specify an amount.

Qatar later blasted the U.N. for treating oil-rich GCC states as bankrollers for its global operations, saying that GCC members had agreed to provide the commission with funds but proportional to the six states' general U.N. quotas.
The GCC fought alongside the 1991 United States-led coalition that liberated Kuwait from a seven-month Iraqi occupation but members like Oman and Qatar have since improved links with Baghdad.
